title.en: Consumer price index (cost of living index)

body.en: A *consumer price index* measures the average change in the retail prices of goods and services bought by a particular class of people (industrial workers, agricultural labourers, urban employees). Steps: decide the class and area, conduct a family budget enquiry to find the items and their weights, collect retail prices, and compute the index. Methods: aggregate expenditure method $\text{CPI} = \frac{\sum p_1 q_0}{\sum p_0 q_0} \times 100$, and family budget method $\text{CPI} = \frac{\sum IW}{\sum W}$, where $I = \frac{p_1}{p_0} \times 100$ and $W = p_0 q_0$ or the budget share.

points.en: Class of people and area are fixed first
Weights from a family budget enquiry
Both methods give the same answer when W = p₀q₀

narration.en: A consumer price index measures the change in the cost of living of one class of people. It is found by the aggregate expenditure method or by the family budget method, sigma I W over sigma W.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. Group indices: Food 180, Clothing 150, Fuel & light 160, House rent 140, Misc. 120; weights 50, 10, 10, 15, 15. Find the CPI. If a worker earned ₹32,000 in the current year, find his real wage.

say.en: Let us work this out together. Group indices: Food 180, Clothing 150, Fuel & light 160, House rent 140, Misc. 120; weights 50, 10, 10, 15, 15. Find the CPI. If a worker earned 32,000 rupees in the current year, find his real wage.
CPI equals 16,000 over 100 equals 160.
Real wage equals 32,000 times 100 over 160 equals 20,000 rupees.
So the answer is CPI equals 160; real wage equals 20,000 rupees.

narration.en: Recap. CPI measures change in the cost of living of a class of people. Aggregate expenditure method: Σp₁q₀/Σp₀q₀ × 100. Family budget method: ΣIW/ΣW. Real wage = money wage × 100/CPI.
